summary.text: A 10-year-old girl presented with hematochezia, tenesmus and abdominal pain. Workup showed elevated fecal calprotectin of 2030 μg/g, biopsy findings of chronic inflammation, and a 6-cm segment of terminal ileal inflammation with mild rectal involvement on computed tomography enterography. She was diagnosed with Crohn's disease (Paris A1b, L3, L4a, B1, G0) and started on adalimumab.

Adalimumab was given as 80 mg then 40 mg 2 weeks later, then 20 mg every 2 weeks, and escalated to 40 mg every 2 weeks for persistent inflammation and a suboptimal level of 7.6 μg/mL. The level was 11.3 μg/mL one year later with transient improvement, but inflammation persisted and repeat endoscopies confirmed chronic active gastritis, duodenitis and ileitis with focal granulomata. Given inadequate response she transitioned to ustekinumab.

The first IV loading dose of ustekinumab 260 mg was followed by a transient erythematous infusion-site rash, and one SQ injection was tolerated 8 weeks later. After 4 months without ustekinumab because of insurance gaps, a one-time 260 mg IV re-induction was begun at an outside hospital; within 30 s she developed acute respiratory distress with facial cyanosis and dyspnea. The infusion was discontinued, intramuscular epinephrine, oxygen and fluids were given, and symptoms completely resolved with observation.

Laboratory evaluation 2 months later showed mild iron deficiency anemia (hemoglobin 11.4 g/dL), elevated ESR (59) and CRP 6.8, negative ustekinumab antibody testing with no detectable drug level, and negative α-gal testing. With the family, SQ ustekinumab was chosen; it was given in office without pre-medication, monitored for 30 min and well tolerated without adverse reactions.
